Theories were circulating for months who JCF would coach, and none of them involved Shelton. On a recent episode of his Served podcast, Andy Roddick offers added motivation for JCF to coach Shelton. top.title: Three California sumo wrestlers added to World Elite Sumo Tournament in Orlando on Nov. 21
top.description: Professional wrestling star and sumo veteran, “Juicy Finau” (left), a massive, 6-foot-4, 465-pound competitor, will return to action at the World Elite Sumo event in Orlando on Saturday, Nov. 21. California will be well represented when World Elite Sumo (WES) returns to Orlando, Florida, later this month. Three California-based competitors—professional wrestler Juicy Finau of Chino, Josh "Siua" Tuitupou of Union City and Gilberto "El Coloso Aztec" De La Torre of Los Angeles—were among seven additional wrestlers announced Wednesday for WES' one-night, 12-man, open-weight tournament at Caribe Royale Orlando on Saturday, Nov. 21. The trio joins previously announced California competitor Makini "Big Mak" Manu of Carson, bringing the state's representation to four wrestlers. Finau, 30, is one of the largest competitors in the tournament, standing 6-foot-4 and weighing 465 pounds. The son of parents from the Kingdom of Tonga, Finau has five years of experience in Greco-Roman and freestyle wrestling, along with a professional wrestling career that has included appearances for AAA Lucha Libre and Major League Wrestling. Finau is also familiar with WES competition, having participated in the organization's Sept. 26 tournament in Santa Cruz, California, where he faced Manu in a matchup between two competitors weighing a combined 865 pounds. Tuitupou, meanwhile, returns to WES competition with a background in Muay Thai. The Union City wrestler, who weighs 268 pounds, utilizes a sumo style that emphasizes pushing, thrusting and disrupting his opponent's balance. De La Torre, a 400-pound competitor from Los Angeles, brings considerable sumo experience to Orlando. A three-time member of the United States national sumo team, De La Torre is known for his aggressive, forward-pressure style and his ability to establish a right-hand-inside grip on opponents. The three Californians will join Manu, the No. 1-ranked super heavyweight in Dana White's Power Slap organization. The 32-year-old Manu, a former professional football player who stands 6 feet tall and weighs 400 pounds, made his professional sumo debut at WES' Santa Cruz tournament in September. He defeated Finau in his opening matchup, winning two consecutive rounds in the best-of-three contest. The four California wrestlers will face a tournament field featuring competitors with backgrounds in mixed martial arts, Brazilian jiu-jitsu, collegiate wrestling and professional sumo. Other newly announced entrants include Florida competitors Brian Dina and Duke "The Viking" Webb, former collegiate wrestling national champion Jahsua Marsh of New York and returning WES competitor Rui Jr. of Brazil. Previously announced participants include reigning tournament champion Hidenoumi "The Iron Wall" Takuya of Japan and Orlando-based Soslan "Big Bear" Gagloev. WES also announced that Brennen Moorefield and Jakob "Mosin" Alekseyev have withdrawn from the tournament, with Moorefield sidelined by a training injury.

top.title: Calvary Day flag football team beats Woodville-Tompkins to win area title
top.description: The Calvary Day flag football team passed another regular season test with flying colors as the Cavs rolled to a 20-0 win over Woodville-Tompkins to win the Division I Area 3 championship at Islands Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 4th. Nick Grassi's squad was firing on all cylinders once again with an explosive offense led by junior quarterback Page Stewart and a stingy defense that recorded its 11th shutout of the season. The Cavs improved to 16-1 and 8-0 in Area play. Calvary will close out the regular season with non-region games against Richmond Hill, Southeast Bulloch and Bradwell Institute as it prepares for the Division I state playoffs where the Cavs will face an opponent to be determined on Nov. 18. Stewart entered the game with 3,211 yards passing with 58 touchdown passes and 13 interceptions and she wasted not time adding to her season stats. The junior connected with Rily Grassi for a 30-yard scoring strike on the Cavs first possession and later connected with Makayla Modicue ― hitting the senior in stride down the right sideline for a 50-yard touchdown. She later found Sanai Williams for a touchdown pass. Modicue had an interception on the first play from scrimmage after her touchdown and Kylie Singleton preserved the shutout in the second half with an interception in the end zone. Stewart hit a career milestone in the fourth quarter as she reached 10,000 yards passing for her career. "I have to credit my receivers for reaching that mark, 100% it all goes to them," Stewart said. "They run the routes, catch the passes and make the touchdowns, and that makes my job so much easier." It was the first Area title for the Cavs since 2023. Calvary reached the Division 2 state quarterfinals last year where the Cavs lost to eventual state champion Greenbrier and coach Nick Grassi thinks his squad has the firepower for another deep run. "It was great to see Page reach that mark tonight," Grassi said. "She is always so level headed ― she never gets too high or too low and that's what our team needs. If we keep playing with this kind of momentum, we should accomplish our goal and that's nothing short of playing in the Dome (for the state championship)." top.description: El Segundo, CA, USA; Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) talks with coach Jim Harbaugh during training camp at The Bolt. EL SEGUNDO, Calif. — The Los Angeles Chargers entered the 2026 season with expectations of competing for a Super Bowl. With the Super Bowl scheduled to be played at SoFi Stadium, the hope was that the Chargers would have an opportunity to compete for a championship in their own building. Instead, their season has turned into a nightmare. Entering Week 9, the Chargers are sitting at 0-7, and their biggest concern is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore: Justin Herbert is playing some of the worst football of his career. Through seven games, Herbert has thrown 10 interceptions, a troubling number for a quarterback who entered the season with expectations of leading this team on a deep playoff run. The turnovers have become part of a much larger offensive problem, one that doesn't appear to be getting any better. The Chargers' offense has gone 27 consecutive drives without scoring a touchdown. That is the longest such streak since the Miami Dolphins went 30 drives without a touchdown in 2024, also under offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. Herbert has five touchdowns and has been sacked 23 times. For an offense with Herbert under center, those numbers are difficult to comprehend. The offensive operation has looked stale, inconsistent and increasingly predictable. There hasn't been much evidence of meaningful improvement, and with the bye week already behind them, it seems unlikely that the Chargers will make any significant coaching changes. If the organization was considering a shake-up, the bye week would have been the most logical opportunity. Instead, head coach Jim Harbaugh continues to publicly defend his quarterback and his offensive staff. Jim Harbaugh responds to Quentin Lake's criticism of Justin Herbert The conversation surrounding Herbert took another turn after Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake made comments questioning the quarterback's decision-making after their 24-9 loss to the Rams last Sunday. Lake's remarks reportedly included a reference to Herbert throwing deli meat and seeing ghosts during the Chargers' loss. When Harbaugh was asked about Lake's criticism, he wasn't particularly interested in entertaining the discussion. "Everybody's entitled to their opinion, that's not what I see," Harbaugh said. Harbaugh went on to defend Herbert's performance, suggesting that the quarterback played exceptionally well outside of two throws he would undoubtedly like to have back. "His pass game, I thought he did his job exceptionally well. Two throws he'd like to have back." That's certainly a generous assessment considering the team's current record and the offensive struggles that have followed Herbert throughout the season. top.title: Tennessee is the final boss for ending the Old Kentucky Football trope
top.description: In just one year, Will Stein has helped Kentucky Football reach heights never seen in Lexington before. The biggest indicator of this came during Tuesday’s debut of the College Football Playoff Selection Committee Rankings, which had Kentucky earning its highest ranking ever at No. 6 . We also cannot forget all of the good his predecessor, Mark Stoops, did in Lexington during his 13-year run as the program’s head coach. Those two have helped nearly vanquish the ‘Old Kentucky Football’ trope that plagued this program for far too long. But for all the good we’ve seen them accomplish, Old Kentucky Football hasn’t been fully eradicated just yet. And these Wildcats have a chance to end a major part of that dreaded trope: Beating a good Tennessee team. Huh? Surely Kentucky has done that against a program it’s played in 83 consecutive seasons Unfortunately, you have to go back quite a ways to find a year Kentucky actually beat a good Volunteers team. You probably remember how the Vols once owned a 26-game winning streak in this series, which finally ended in 2011. And while Tennessee has still owned this series since then, the Wildcats do have two other wins since then in 2017 and 2020. In fact, that 2020 win in Knoxville was over an 18th-ranked Tennessee squad that’s not too far from this week’s 13th-ranked Volunteers team. However, that Tennessee team turned out to be a disaster, finishing 3-7 before having the entire season vacated due to recruiting violations. Kentucky’s 2017 win wasn’t much better. Those Vols finished 4-8 and fired head coach Butch Jones just two weeks after losing in Lexington. The 2011 Tennessee team at least had a chance to make a bowl game. The Vols entered the regular-season finale matchup with Kentucky at 5-6 overall, but the Matt Roark-led Wildcats scored an improbable 10-7 victory to send Derek Dooley’s Vols home for the holidays at 5-7. You won’t find another Kentucky win in the series until you get all the way back to 1984, when a 9-3 Wildcats squad went into Knoxville and took down a Tennessee team that finished 7-4-1. That’s the last time Kentucky beat a Vols team that finished with a winning record. Ironically, that Kentucky team featured defensive end Matt Stein, the father of first-year head coach Will Stein . Yes, that means UK’s 37-year-old coach, along with many of us, wasn’t even alive to see the last time Kentucky actually beat a good Tennessee team. top.title: Mizzou Eli Drinkwitz Shuts Down Florida State Rumors
top.description: FAYETTEVILLE, ARKANSAS - OCTOBER 31: Head Coach Eli Drinkwitz of the Missouri Tigers looks at the camera in the rain before the game against the Arkansas Razorbacks at Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Fayetteville, Arkansas. (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) Getty The Missouri Tigers are entering the toughest stretch of their season, which has already included three top-25 opponents, with two of them coming on the road. The last thing that Mizzou head coach Eli Drinkwitz wants in his building is distraction. He quickly dismissed any rumors of his connection to the Florida State job opening after Mike Norvell was fired on Sunday. “I’m not a candidate at Florida State,” Drinkwitz said in his presser on Tuesday. “Let’s clear that up.” Every coaching carousel season, rumors flurry that Drinkwitz could be a candidate for a top job elsewhere. Last season it was Penn State and Florida. This season, it begins with the first major opening in college football. Eli Drinkwitz Wants Distraction-Free Environment Ahead Of Texas The Tigers begin a three-week gauntlet this week with the Texas Longhorns coming to Columbia, Missouri, and Drinkwitz wants his team to have a distraction-free environment. Drinkwitz made an emphasis on focusing on Texa s and not any of the other distractions that come with a high profile job opening up. This same song and dance comes around at this point every season that a premier job opens in college football. Whether that is for Drinkwitz or another coach in a spot to make a jump to a major player in the Power 4. Drinkwitz has been committed to Missouri since he stepped on campus to become the head coach in 2020, and turned a lackluster Missouri program into a regular in the top 25. Missouri’s Final Stretch Provides Path To College Football Playoffs The Tigers debut in the College Football Playoff rankings at No. 18, with three top-10 teams remaining on their schedule. The next three weeks will determine where Missouri stands in contention for a potential playoff berth. First up in No. 7 Texas, which is an old Big 12 rivalry renewed and a Texas team that has already suffered a pair of disappointing defeats this season. Following that, the Tigers head to face No. 3 Georgia before returning home to battle an upstart No. 6 Kentucky. The Tigers will then wrap up their season with the Oklahoma Sooners in Columbia. Missouri sitting at two losses already on the season, will have take care of business on their road. They might be able to suffer just one more loss with their tough schedule, but any more than that and they are certainly out of the playoffs. With Drinkwitz shutting down all rumors of a potential move to Florida State, the Tigers can focus on the task at hand. Missouri will look to take this final month one game at a time and put themselves in the best position come Selection Sunday. top.title: Haaland eyes 'lots of things' Man City can improve after Leipzig win
top.description: Manchester City's Erling Haaland celebrates scoring his side's third goal during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between RB Leipzig and Manchester City at Red Bull Arena. (is associated with: «Haaland eyes 'lots of things' Man City can improve after Leipzig win») Robert Michael/dpa Erling Haaland called on Manchester City to become more ruthless after twice being pegged back before beating RB Leipzig 3-2 on Wednesday. Haaland scored a 78th-minute winner as City finally saw off the German side in their Champions League league phase clash at the Red Bull Arena. Haaland felt City should have been more aggressive and killed the game off much earlier. "I think we need to step up a little bit," the Norwegian told TNT Sports. "I think when we were 1-0, I think we needed to push forward a bit more to go at it, go for the second and then hopefully go for the third. "That's what we have to do as a club. We have to work on that." Asked what areas the team could improve, Haaland added: "I think keeping the ball, when to keep it, when to go, working together, both offensively, defensively. Lots of different things. "That's the good part, you can always get better, and there's always a new chance, and now there will be a new game in three days, so that's lovely." City led after a Castello Lukeba own goal before half-time but that was cancelled out early in the second period by Ridle Baku. Enzo Fernandez restored City's lead but the impressive Antonio Nusa equalized again for Leipzig. Haaland had a quiet night until arriving at the back post to slide in the winner from Elliot Anderson's superb ball. It was just his 13th touch of the game. He said: "It's not the most but what is the most important is I help the team to win, and I managed to do that, so I'm super happy." It was Haaland's 14th goal of the season and a 13th in nine career appearances against Leipzig for the former Borussia Dortmund striker. He said: "I think it's the most I've scored against a club because I've played so many times against them. "As well in the Champions League with City every year I was in Dortmund as well. Leipzig are a good team, so I'm super happy about that." Manager Enzo Maresca was pleased with his players' response after Saturday's loss to Brighton, which was their second in succession in the Premier League. Maresca said: "I'm happy with the win. That is important, especially after a defeat. "I think part of the game we controlled quite well, creating many chances. Then for some moments, we struggled a little bit but that's normal, it's a Champions League game. It's Germany away. "It's always difficult, so we're happy with the win."

nigeria.description: … Women record twice men’s prevalence as state targets wider coverage By Chioma Obinna Lagos State has recorded significant progress in HIV treatment, with 93.4 per cent of people living with the virus who know their status receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART), a new survey has revealed. nigeria.title: Google turns off AI for schoolchildren by default
nigeria.description: Google has said it will switch off its AI tools for schoolchildren by default, after drawing criticism for pushing artificial intelligence features to students while schools are still debating how the technology should be used in classrooms. The search engine juggernaut dominates technology in American schools. Its education apps, including Gmail, Docs and the Classroom platform, are used in classrooms across the country, and its low-cost Chromebook laptops are the devices US schools most often issue to students. Under the changes Google announced in a blog post on Tuesday, Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Search will be turned off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators switch them on. Google told AFP the new controls would be rolled out worldwide, beginning in the United States, but that it had not yet set a date. The changes also mean schools will not be able to give students Google Search without its AI features. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president for education, told The New York Times that “Search and A.I. are deeply integrated,” as AI features are now built into the company’s search engine. If a school bans AI, he said, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.” New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google on X of “trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools.” “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children,” he wrote. More than 150 million students worldwide use Google Classroom, according to a letter Senators Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley sent to the company last month asking why AI features had been made the default on school devices. In August, Google opened its Gemini chatbot in Classroom to students of all ages. Students were shown starter prompts tied to their specific class and assignment, offering guided help or study guides, practice quizzes and flashcards built from their course materials. The feature was switched on by default for students at schools that had already enabled Gemini. New York and Los Angeles both announced plans in September to restrict access to AI tools on school devices. “We are reviewing Google’s announcement and its potential implications for schools, educators and students,” a spokesperson for the Los Angeles Unified School District told AFP. The spokesperson said the district believes AI can improve teaching and learning if it is introduced carefully and with clear safeguards, and pointed to district principles requiring that technology support rather than replace teachers and protect student privacy. In a statement on X, Google said Tuesday’s changes give “schools more choice, not less.” “We know there’s concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork, and schools have told us they want control,” Google said. nigeria.description: By Innocent Anaba The Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, will chair the public presentation of six legal books authored by Dr ‘Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, on November 20, 2026. The publications, which draw on Pinheiro’s nearly four decades of legal practice, examine critical areas of Nigerian law, including criminal litigation, arbitration, corporate insolvency, justice administration and emerging legal issues. The collection comprises Strategies in Criminal Trial: A Practitioner’s Guide; Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure; Arbitration Law and Practice in Nigeria; Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk (Volume One); The Compendium; and MULAN Legal: Trending Issues of Law and Faith – Essays in Honour of ‘Kemi Pinheiro, SAN. The book on criminal trials examines key procedural and evidential issues in criminal proceedings, including the treatment and admissibility of electronic evidence. Similarly, Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure explores the legal framework governing corporate rescue, restructuring and insolvency proceedings under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020. Arbitration Law and Practice in Nigeria examines the country’s arbitration framework, with particular attention to the Arbitration and Mediation Act 2023 and the enforcement of arbitral awards. U.S. District Judge Valerie Caproni denied the temporary restraining order on Nov. 3 after a teleconference with the parties, hours after the CFTC said the products could begin trading on U.S.-regulated exchanges. The plaintiff is the Capital Markets Alliance Association, a New York nonprofit whose members include Cboe Global Markets, Citadel Securities and the Healthy Markets Association, according to a declaration from its secretary, Adam Ford. The group sued the CFTC and Chairman Michael S. Selig in the Southern District of New York, case No. 1:26-cv-09608, seeking to undo the approvals of filings by all three exchanges. Caproni wrote that the group “is likely to succeed on the merits” of its claim that the agency lacks statutory authority to allow perpetual derivatives on individual stocks to be offered to retail investors on CFTC-regulated platforms. “Because the perpetual contracts, by definition, do not provide for a ‘sale for future delivery of a single security,’ they cannot be a security future over which the CFTC has statutory and regulatory authority,” she wrote. Instead, she said, the contracts “appear to satisfy the definition of a swap,” which falls to the Securities and Exchange Commission. She also found that the balance of equities and the public interest favor the alliance, writing that the agency’s actions “seem to represent a major disruption to the equities market.” The request failed on one prong. Bitcoin positions accounted for $403 million of the total, 76% of it shorts. entertainment.description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa: African Philanthropy Forum (APF) closed its 2026 Conference in Cape Town on 27 October with a message that ran through nearly every session: Africa’s challenges are connected, so African giving has to be connected too. Held from 25 to 27 October under the theme Bridge the Divide; Reimagine the Future , the conference brought together philanthropists, funders, business leaders, creatives, and technologists to ask how African capital can be mobilized, how partnerships can be strengthened, and how African-led solutions can be backed with more trust and flexibility. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. sports.title: Three California sumo wrestlers added to World Elite Sumo Tournament in Orlando on Nov. 21
sports.description: Professional wrestling star and sumo veteran, “Juicy Finau” (left), a massive, 6-foot-4, 465-pound competitor, will return to action at the World Elite Sumo event in Orlando on Saturday, Nov. 21. California will be well represented when World Elite Sumo (WES) returns to Orlando, Florida, later this month. Three California-based competitors—professional wrestler Juicy Finau of Chino, Josh "Siua" Tuitupou of Union City and Gilberto "El Coloso Aztec" De La Torre of Los Angeles—were among seven additional wrestlers announced Wednesday for WES' one-night, 12-man, open-weight tournament at Caribe Royale Orlando on Saturday, Nov. 21. The trio joins previously announced California competitor Makini "Big Mak" Manu of Carson, bringing the state's representation to four wrestlers. Finau, 30, is one of the largest competitors in the tournament, standing 6-foot-4 and weighing 465 pounds. The son of parents from the Kingdom of Tonga, Finau has five years of experience in Greco-Roman and freestyle wrestling, along with a professional wrestling career that has included appearances for AAA Lucha Libre and Major League Wrestling. Finau is also familiar with WES competition, having participated in the organization's Sept. 26 tournament in Santa Cruz, California, where he faced Manu in a matchup between two competitors weighing a combined 865 pounds. Tuitupou, meanwhile, returns to WES competition with a background in Muay Thai. The Union City wrestler, who weighs 268 pounds, utilizes a sumo style that emphasizes pushing, thrusting and disrupting his opponent's balance. De La Torre, a 400-pound competitor from Los Angeles, brings considerable sumo experience to Orlando. A three-time member of the United States national sumo team, De La Torre is known for his aggressive, forward-pressure style and his ability to establish a right-hand-inside grip on opponents. The three Californians will join Manu, the No. 1-ranked super heavyweight in Dana White's Power Slap organization. The 32-year-old Manu, a former professional football player who stands 6 feet tall and weighs 400 pounds, made his professional sumo debut at WES' Santa Cruz tournament in September. He defeated Finau in his opening matchup, winning two consecutive rounds in the best-of-three contest. The four California wrestlers will face a tournament field featuring competitors with backgrounds in mixed martial arts, Brazilian jiu-jitsu, collegiate wrestling and professional sumo. Other newly announced entrants include Florida competitors Brian Dina and Duke "The Viking" Webb, former collegiate wrestling national champion Jahsua Marsh of New York and returning WES competitor Rui Jr. of Brazil. Previously announced participants include reigning tournament champion Hidenoumi "The Iron Wall" Takuya of Japan and Orlando-based Soslan "Big Bear" Gagloev. WES also announced that Brennen Moorefield and Jakob "Mosin" Alekseyev have withdrawn from the tournament, with Moorefield sidelined by a training injury.

sports.title: Calvary Day flag football team beats Woodville-Tompkins to win area title
sports.description: The Calvary Day flag football team passed another regular season test with flying colors as the Cavs rolled to a 20-0 win over Woodville-Tompkins to win the Division I Area 3 championship at Islands Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 4th. Nick Grassi's squad was firing on all cylinders once again with an explosive offense led by junior quarterback Page Stewart and a stingy defense that recorded its 11th shutout of the season. The Cavs improved to 16-1 and 8-0 in Area play. Calvary will close out the regular season with non-region games against Richmond Hill, Southeast Bulloch and Bradwell Institute as it prepares for the Division I state playoffs where the Cavs will face an opponent to be determined on Nov. 18. Stewart entered the game with 3,211 yards passing with 58 touchdown passes and 13 interceptions and she wasted not time adding to her season stats. The junior connected with Rily Grassi for a 30-yard scoring strike on the Cavs first possession and later connected with Makayla Modicue ― hitting the senior in stride down the right sideline for a 50-yard touchdown. She later found Sanai Williams for a touchdown pass. Modicue had an interception on the first play from scrimmage after her touchdown and Kylie Singleton preserved the shutout in the second half with an interception in the end zone. Stewart hit a career milestone in the fourth quarter as she reached 10,000 yards passing for her career. "I have to credit my receivers for reaching that mark, 100% it all goes to them," Stewart said. "They run the routes, catch the passes and make the touchdowns, and that makes my job so much easier." It was the first Area title for the Cavs since 2023. Calvary reached the Division 2 state quarterfinals last year where the Cavs lost to eventual state champion Greenbrier and coach Nick Grassi thinks his squad has the firepower for another deep run. "It was great to see Page reach that mark tonight," Grassi said. "She is always so level headed ― she never gets too high or too low and that's what our team needs. If we keep playing with this kind of momentum, we should accomplish our goal and that's nothing short of playing in the Dome (for the state championship)." sports.title: Jim Harbaugh isn't ready to admit there's a problem with Justin Herbert
sports.description: El Segundo, CA, USA; Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) talks with coach Jim Harbaugh during training camp at The Bolt. EL SEGUNDO, Calif. — The Los Angeles Chargers entered the 2026 season with expectations of competing for a Super Bowl. With the Super Bowl scheduled to be played at SoFi Stadium, the hope was that the Chargers would have an opportunity to compete for a championship in their own building. Instead, their season has turned into a nightmare. Entering Week 9, the Chargers are sitting at 0-7, and their biggest concern is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore: Justin Herbert is playing some of the worst football of his career. Through seven games, Herbert has thrown 10 interceptions, a troubling number for a quarterback who entered the season with expectations of leading this team on a deep playoff run. The turnovers have become part of a much larger offensive problem, one that doesn't appear to be getting any better. The Chargers' offense has gone 27 consecutive drives without scoring a touchdown. That is the longest such streak since the Miami Dolphins went 30 drives without a touchdown in 2024, also under offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. Herbert has five touchdowns and has been sacked 23 times. For an offense with Herbert under center, those numbers are difficult to comprehend. The offensive operation has looked stale, inconsistent and increasingly predictable. There hasn't been much evidence of meaningful improvement, and with the bye week already behind them, it seems unlikely that the Chargers will make any significant coaching changes. If the organization was considering a shake-up, the bye week would have been the most logical opportunity. Instead, head coach Jim Harbaugh continues to publicly defend his quarterback and his offensive staff. Jim Harbaugh responds to Quentin Lake's criticism of Justin Herbert The conversation surrounding Herbert took another turn after Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake made comments questioning the quarterback's decision-making after their 24-9 loss to the Rams last Sunday. Lake's remarks reportedly included a reference to Herbert throwing deli meat and seeing ghosts during the Chargers' loss. When Harbaugh was asked about Lake's criticism, he wasn't particularly interested in entertaining the discussion. "Everybody's entitled to their opinion, that's not what I see," Harbaugh said. Harbaugh went on to defend Herbert's performance, suggesting that the quarterback played exceptionally well outside of two throws he would undoubtedly like to have back. sports.description: Massive conflict between Nikita Kucherov and Victor Hedman surfaces amid trade bombshell The hockey world was rocked over the weekend when Nikita Kucherov, one of the most dominant forwards in the NHL, officially requested a trade out of Tampa Bay. But the bombshell trade demand may only be scratching the surface of a much deeper fracture inside the Lightning organization. According to Elliotte Friedman of Sportsnet, Kucherov informed Tampa Bay's front office that he has no intention of signing an extension and wants out. General manager Julien BriseBois confirmed the situation through an official statement, though he made clear the team does not plan to move its star before the end of the current season. The real shock, however, came from behind closed doors. Martin McGuire, the play-by-play voice of the Montreal Canadiens, revealed on 98.5 Sports that a significant rift exists between Kucherov and captain Victor Hedman. According to McGuire, the two players are simply unable to coexist, on the ice or off it. "Kucherov is in conflict with Victor Hedman. The two aren't really able to go out to dinner together on the road, I can tell you that," McGuire said. "I think it's something that's fairly well known around the NHL and around the Lightning. Jon Cooper isn't going to go public to talk about these things, but Hedman and Kucherov, you wouldn't invite them to the same party." https://x.com/985Sports/status/2117425845916573826?a=7gyeXseW2YF_Iu9-Nz4&s=20 Kucherov himself broke his silence during a brief media availability, and he was emphatic that money is not driving his decision. technology.description: AI has become a juggernaut, driving technical strategy in the tech sector and outside of it. With the worldwide server market growing 30 percent in a single year to hit $122.6bn in the first quarter of 2025, IDC now feels safe recategorizing AI-driven investment "from cyclical to durable". The analyst company expects inference to account for over 70 percent of computing demand by next year, adding that it's growing fastest at the edge. Why enterprises are building their own All this investment in AI infrastructure might once have come mainly for hyperscalers, but that's changing quickly. Adoption is spreading quickly beyond public cloud service providers into enterprise environments, IDC adds. They're eager to run agentic AI in-house. There are plenty of reasons for companies to own their own AI infrastructure rather than offloading it to the cloud. One of these is data control, especially in regulated sectors such as finance, healthcare, manufacturing, and the public sector that have sovereign data requirements. Another revolves around the need for predictable costing from tokens delivered on tunable in-house systems. So what should companies look for in a supplier? Delivery speed will be a powerful driver for many who are under the gun to deliver AI initiatives for the business, especially during periods of constrained memory and CPU supply. Life cycle services will also come near the top of the list, for companies that need help managing everything from the power through to the reasoning LLM models and the workloads that use them. That need for expertise is unlikely to stop; companies will undergo changes in AI strategy as they get to grips with a still-evolving technology. From the desk to the datacenter ASUS expects this AI surge to continue in the datacenter, but elsewhere too, specifically in edge locations (especially industrial use cases) and at developers' desks, as the applications that will power the enterprise get made. It wants to be top of peoples' list for hardware and services at all these places along the AI continuum. At NVIDIA's GTC show in Berlin on Oct 21-22, it announced a full-stack AI offering that it's calling its Enterprise Agentic AI Solution . It's three-layer affair, featuring: ASUS AI Server and Infrastructure: Its selection of AI servers, including several new units. technology.title: Nintendo's biggest ROM chip supplier is bowing out of the business
technology.description: For years, the AI industry's insatiable demand for memory and storage has had plenty of knock-on effects on the price and availability of PC components like RAM , SSDs , and GPUs . Now those shortages are also squeezing the supply of ROM chips that power physical Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 game cartridges. Chip manufacturer Macronix announced in its third-quarter earnings report that the company's production of ROM chips "has reached its end" and that it will begin "gradually decoupling from the game industry," as reported by Taiwanese news site BigGo Finance . That could be an issue for Nintendo, which analyst David Gibson notes uses Macronix as its "main memory chip maker" for physical game cartridges. That ROM production—which has shrunk 39 percent in the last year and now represents just 5 percent of Macronix's business—is being crowded out by production of more lucrative, in-demand chips like NOR- and NAND-based memory and eMMCs, the company said. With Macronix's production capacity stuck at 25,000 12-inch wafers a month—and $1.2 billion in planned new capacity taking a year or more to spin up—less profitable ROM chips are taking up wafer space that can earn more through other types of chips. technology.title: Uranium cubes reveal why the German nuclear project failed
technology.description: During World War II, physicists on the Manhattan Project worried that the Nazi German nuclear program might achieve the first nuclear bomb before the US and its allies. That's not what transpired, but historians have debated just how close the Germans came to achieving criticality in their last attempt at building a reactor: the B8 pile. Werner Heisenberg, who led that effort, claimed that they were close and had only needed a little more uranium. But according to a paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences Nexus, that was not the case: the project simply didn't have sufficient uranium and heavy water to build a working bomb, given the design they were using. This particular research started in 2013, when University of Maryland physicist Timothy Koeth—a co-author on the new paper—received the gift of a mysterious heavy metal cube from a friend. He instantly recognized it as one of the uranium cubes used by German scientists in their unsuccessful attempt to build a working nuclear reactor. Only 14 such cubes are known to exist today. In 2019, we reported on Koeth’s quest to track down the cube’s origins, as well as several other similar cubes that had somehow found their way across the Atlantic. At the time, Koeth and his partner in the quest, then-graduate student Miriam “Mimi” Hiebert, had tracked down ten such cubes around the US. For instance, the Smithsonian Institute had a German uranium cube in storage. They tracked a third cube to Harvard University, where it was regularly passed around to students in introductory physics classes as a curiosity. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Apple turns iCloud into spy cloud, will start looking at public share links
technology.description: If you share content using public iCloud links, Apple could soon be looking over your shoulder and checking for "harmful content." The iBiz announced plans to moderate publicly accessible iCloud share links in version 27.3 of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS on a support page published on Tuesday. To clarify, this applies only to iCloud content shared via links created to be accessible to anyone, as opposed to content shared directly with other people. “Items shared using Anyone with the Link will be checked by Apple for harmful content,” Apple explained on the new help page without bothering to define what harmful content means. Based on the wording, it appears those checks will apply to all iCloud items shared using "Anyone with the Link," which Apple says it can also access. The company hasn't explained how the checks will work. The share-with-anyone option removes end-to-end encryption from the shared item, Apple said, even if Advanced Data Protection , Apple's optional end-to-end encryption feature for supported iCloud data, remains enabled for the account. “If you try to upload harmful content, Apple reserves the right to move, refuse, modify, remove, or delete the content at any time,” the help page continues, adding that the iMaker may also block or disable accounts associated with harmful content. The company also said it reserves the right to involve law enforcement when necessary, suggesting that its undefined "harmful content" category could include child sexual abuse material (CSAM), malware, and other potentially unlawful content. Without a proper definition of what it defines as harmful, however, iCloud users are essentially left at Apple’s mercy: If it chooses to continue to bend the knee to the Trump administration, for example, content deemed objectionable by the standards of political figures could end up wiped out. Apple also hasn't explained whether human moderators, automated systems, or both will be responsible for identifying and removing so-called harmful content, or whether any decisions will be left to AI, which can easily be fooled into making a bad moderation call. The scanning of such content, as mentioned above, begins with version 27.3 of Apple’s various OSes, which were released to developers in beta on Tuesday, with a general release expected in December. Apple didn’t respond to questions for this story. ®

technology.title: Hey, Siri: Plug into my app like you said you'd do way back in 2024

Next spring, nearly three years after announcing plans for deeper third-party Siri integration, Apple expects to begin accepting App Store submissions using the new capabilities. "This developer beta offers a sneak peek at Siri AI app intents for developers," Apple said in a developer news post . "With this early Developer Preview, your app can work directly with Siri AI, giving you a first look at new ways to reach and serve your customers." Anything is likely to be an improvement. Apple's Siri, a voice-activated assistant service, dates back to 2011 and gained limited third-party app access in 2016. In 2024, it became an interface for interacting with Apple Intelligence, its suite of generative AI features. Apple Intelligence has not been very intelligent – several advertised Siri capabilities were delayed, so much so that Apple was sued in 2025 over allegations of misleading marketing. After a shakeup of Apple's machine learning group in December 2025, Siri and Apple Intelligence received a makeover at Apple's Worldwide Developers Conference in June. "Before this year, Siri was a timer with a voice," said Roberto Gutierrez, Apple platforms staff engineer at a media company and author of the e-book On-Device Intelligence, in an email to The Register . "Weather, alarms, calls. Anything past that was a coin toss. "On the developer side, SiriKit covered a handful of domains and Shortcuts only worked if users memorized the phrase. Siri AI is the first version that understands context and can chain actions across apps. That's a real change." There is a catch, however, Gutierrez observed. Siri AI is available in a limited number of languages and regions. Support for Traditional Chinese is expected by the end of 2026, and EU availability remains a matter of negotiation – Siri AI is unavailable on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS in the bloc as Apple works through interoperability concerns under Europe's Digital Markets Act. "Apple is working constructively with the EU in an attempt to find a path forward," the company said last month without committing to any concessions. Gutierrez said that he expects opening Siri to third-party developers will be useful to some extent. "Siri can only do what apps expose through App Intents, and SiriKit is on its way out," he said. "If your app's main actions aren't exposed, the new Siri can't see you. The bigger shift is letting Claude, Gemini and others plug in. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
science.description: null On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan . For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket . The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff. Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor. The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms. After failing to launch this batch of cubesats, the Super Strypi program never recovered from its failure, and the Air Force never tried launching another one. The U.S. Air Force’s rail-launched Super Strypi rocket lifted off from Hawaii about 9:45 p.m. local time on Nov. 3, 2015,, roared toward the sky and failed less than a minute into the long-awaited flight. (Image credit: U.S. Air Force) Why it mattered The Super Strypi rocket was a 21st century take on a 1960s rocket. It was designed to be a modern version of the three-stage Strypi sounding rocket used for for reentry vehicle and anti-missile target tests. Its three stages, powered by Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motors, was designed to reach orbit, rather than suborbital trajectories common to most sounding rockets. The U.S. Air Force hoped Super Strypi would be a new tool for quick-response launches based on national security needs. Altogether, it was designed to launch small payloads of up to 300 kilograms into space for a mere $15 million per mission . The rocket's primary payload was the ORS-4 satellite, short for Operationally Responsive Space 4, which was built for the Air Force by engineers at the University of Hawaii (who nicknamed it HiakaSat). It was designed to capture Earth imagery and monitor the environment over the course of a year. The 12 other payloads on Super Strypi included eight cubesats for NASA's Edison Demonstration of Smallsat Networks mission, and as well as four others for universities that had been added as secondary payloads. Since the Super Strypi failure, neither the Air Force or Space Force has opted to use the rocket for a new mission. The Space Force has turned instead to commercial companies for fast-turnaround launch support. In June of this year, the U.S. Space Force teamed up with Rocket Lab to launch the Victus Haze mission with just 17 hours of notice , a new record to demonstrate short-turnaround launch response.

science.title: Trump declares 'American space superiority for all eternity' in election night proclamation
science.description: null President Trump issued a declaration yesterday (Nov. 3), proclaiming space open to all humanity for exploration, and the right of American citizens to develop and settle the solar system according to United States laws. "The American Declaration of Freedom in Space," describes space as the "province of all humans" and asserts that the United States will lead humanity's expansion into the cosmos. The proclamation reiterates the administration's goals with NASA's Artemis program to return American astronauts to the moon by 2028 and eventually sending astronauts to Mars , but introduces no new funding, programs or policy directives. "Our Nation will lead the way in the exploration, development, use, and settlement of these new frontiers — forging an interplanetary civilization founded on the enduring and inalienable rights of freedom and individual liberty," the document says. Trump invoked America's "frontier spirit," highlighting Apollo 11 astronauts as the first people in history to walk on the moon's surface and robotic rovers exploring Mars as examples of U.S. leadership, and emphasized the country's flourishing commercial space sector helping ensure "American space superiority for all eternity." "The nation that leads in space will shape the future of humanity," the declaration says, and pledges that America will carry the values of faith, freedom and individual liberty into an interplanetary civilization. The proclamation also highlights the success of NASA's Artemis II mission in April, which carried four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon and set a record for the farthest humans have ever traveled from Earth . The follow-up to that mission, Artemis III, is scheduled to launch next summer (2027), and will test rendezvous and docking operations between NASA's Orion spacecraft and the program's two commercial lunar landers in low Earth orbit . Artemis IV will be the program's first lunar landing mission, and is targeted for 2028. A December 2025 executive order from the President reaffirmed the goal of meeting that timeline, as well as the deployment of the initial elements for a permanent lunar outpost by 2030. Trump's declaration yesterday does not establish new NASA programs, allocate additional funding or issue instructions to federal agencies. Its sweeping language, though, does echo some of the principles in the 1967 Outer Space Treaty , which guarantees freedom of exploration while prohibiting national sovereignty claims on other planets.

science.title: NASA's Swift space telescope crashes back to Earth after failed rescue attempt
science.description: null NASA's Swift space telescope has reached the end of its long and winding road. Swift fell uncontrolled to Earth today (Nov. 4), 22 years after it launched but just three months after a private spacecraft was supposed to boost it to a higher, life-extending orbit. The 3,200-pound (1,450 kilograms) observatory reentered Earth's atmosphere at 7:39 a.m. EST (1239 GMT) today over northern Sumatra, according to satellite tracker Jonathan McDowell , who cited U.S. Space Force data. The fall likely didn't make much of an impact; NASA officials predicted beforehand that most of the minibus-sized Swift would burn up as it fell, and they put the odds of any of the surviving pieces hurting anyone on Earth at just 1 in 2,100. Swift — officially known as the Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Explorer — launched to Earth orbit in November 2004 on a two-year mission to study gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), the most powerful explosions in the universe . "Swift" was not an acronym but rather referred to the spacecraft's observational agility. "Swift needed to detect and locate gamma-ray bursts, communicate their position to other observatories, and then swing its telescopes around to image the burst locations before their afterglows faded out," S. Bradley Cenko, Swift's principal investigator (PI) at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland, said in an Oct. 23 statement . "This typically took Swift about a minute to do." Swift didn't just observe GRBs. It also studied a variety of other cosmic bodies and phenomena, from faraway supernova explosions and feeding black holes to asteroids and comets in our own solar system. And it kept doing this long after its warranty expired — for about 20 years after, in fact. The space telescope didn't conduct its final science observation until this past Oct. 20 . (Swift underwent a name change during this stretch: In 2018, it was rechristened the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory after its first PI, who died the previous year.) science.title: Toothbrush that emits electricity may more effectively prevent gum disease
science.description: A new and improved toothbrush could help avoid trips to the dentist Westend61/Alamy A toothbrush that generates electricity may more effectively fight harmful bacteria, while removing plaque, than existing products. The toothbrush uses special bristles that produce electricity as they bend, triggering the formation of molecules that damage bacterial membranes. When put to the test, it led to more than twice the reduction of plaque, gum inflammation and bleeding as conventional toothbrushes. “The concept is great,” says Nicholas Jakubovics at Newcastle University, UK, who wasn’t involved in the research. “Basically, the mechanical forces recharge the surface, so it’s really innovative. Anything that even slightly improves the way dental care works could have a benefit, because oral disease is just so widespread.” Read more How regrowing your own teeth could replace dentures and implants Oral diseases, such as tooth decay, affect nearly half the global population . Brushing regularly can help remove plaque, a sticky layer of bacteria that forms on teeth. These bacteria can produce acids that cause cavities and irritate gums, sometimes leading to tooth loss. Advertisement But even thorough brushing can leave behind bacteria deep in plaque or between teeth, allowing colonies to grow back within hours. Researchers have previously developed toothbrushes with antibacterial metal nanoparticles, including silver and zinc, embedded in their bristles , although their long-term effectiveness is uncertain. Others have designed ionic toothbrushes that use electric currents to help loosen plaque , but they are dependent on batteries. Now, Yanhui Lu at Peking University in China and her colleagues have turned to studies showing that so-called piezoelectric materials fight bacteria in infected wounds and medical implants. These generate electric charges under pressure , prompting Lu’s team to develop toothbrush bristles made from piezoelectric plastic. The researchers made two sets of bristles of different thicknesses, both of which met Chinese national standards for softness and strength. Laboratory tests confirmed the bristles generated electricity under pressure, particularly the thicker ones. science.title: Mars isn't dead — recent volcanic activity reveals it's just sleeping
science.description: null Scientists have long suspected that Mars is geologically "dead," but new spacecraft observations suggest the Red Planet's volcanoes are merely sleeping. That means that Olympus Mons , the extinct Martian volcano that at around 16 miles (26 kilometers) above the surrounding Martian plains is the largest mountain in the solar system , may in fact be a slumbering giant. The observations were made with the European Space Agency (ESA) mission ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) as it studied volcanic fissures along the Alba Mons region of the Red Planet. Alba Mons is in the Tharsis region of Mars, the same area that is home to Olympus Mons. While the latter is the tallest volcano in the solar system, at 374 miles (600 km) across, about the size of Arizona, the Alba Mons region is the largest volcano when considering surface area. TGO detected gas containing hydrogen chloride making its way to the surface of Mars through the Alba Mons fissures. The same gas is commonly found escaping from magmatic vents on Earth, with the compound coming from hot magma beneath the surface. Detecting it on Mars is a sign of dormant Martian volcanism. Orbital imagery had previously shown some volcanoes appear to have been active within the last few million years, and seismometers have detected the rumbling of "marsquakes," both implying the Red Planet is volcanically active. However, eruptions and lava flows have been conspicuous by their absence. "Our findings suggest that Mars has retained enough internal heat to support volcanic activity until recently, and possibly still does," team co-leader and scientist at the Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences, Daniel Mège, said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. "The TGO was able to find the smoking gun. It was like looking for a needle in a haystack." Evidence of dormant Martian volcanism is rising Mège and colleagues were first alerted to something strange happening on Mars when they noticed spikes of hydrogen chloride during Martian summer and on the northern hemisphere of the Red Planet. That is both a time and place at which hydrogen chloride shouldn't be detected. The gas usually peaks in the northern hemisphere during winter on Mars, disappearing in the summer. This variation is connected to the water and dust cycle on Mars. An exception to the rule occurs over volcanic fissures on the flanks of the Alba Mons volcano, in early summer. The TGO followed up on this by detecting fresh and narrow fissures, in some cases hundreds of feet long, in the Alba Mons region. A clear sign of volcanism. "It's truly amazing that it spotted a handful of molecules from a perhaps intermittent source, whilst moving continuously along its orbit to monitor the whole Martian atmosphere," Mège said. science.title: NASA Announces Ka-Band Satellite Relay Awards for Space Communications
science.description: Credit: NASA NASA selected three companies on Wednesday to perform work to develop Ka-band space relay capability concepts that are compatible with current missions in space, ensuring service continuity for existing spacecraft without requiring modifications to their onboard systems. Through this work, NASA will aim to acquire end-to-end solutions that include space, ground, launch, operations, and integration elements, as one of many customers in the commercial marketplace. The awards, under the Next Space Technologies for Exploration Partnerships-3 Broad Agency Announcement Appendix E, are firm-fixed-price contracts that give NASA the option to provide additional funding up to the award limit to advance from initial concept development and risk reduction to an in-orbit flight demonstration. The initial period of performance runs from Nov. 4 through May 3, 2027, with additional priced options to continue work through 2029. The contract awardees with maximum potential value inclusive of all future options are: Astranis Space Technologies Corp. for $264.3 million. Global Enterprise Solutions Inc. for $340.4 million. Viasat Inc. for $460.9 million. Facilitated through the agency’s SCaN (Space Communications and Navigation) program’s Communications Services Project, this work supports NASA’s decision to gradually retire the Tracking and Data Relay Satellite fleet and adopt commercial services for future missions. In addition to the commercial capabilities currently under development by the program’s industry partners, Ka-band services are needed to support select in-orbit missions that cannot feasibly modify flight hardware or transition to non-compatible commercial services. A dyslexia diagnosis can help struggling children, but what about the rest?
science.description: Shutterstock/Jakub Krechowicz In years gone by, children who struggled to learn to read and spell were labelled “stupid”, “lazy” or “dim”. Today, of course, we are much more enlightened – now we label many of these children as “dyslexic”. But perhaps this label is still a bad idea. Picture two 9-year-olds reading at the level of an average 6-year-old. One gets a diagnosis of dyslexia. This positively affects her wellbeing. Her teachers now understand she has dyslexia and that she can get tailored help. The other child isn’t so lucky. Maybe his parents can’t afford a dyslexia test – in the UK, assessment isn’t available on the NHS and can cost several hundred pounds. In the US it could set parents back thousands of dollars. Or perhaps he was tested but the result was negative. Until very recently, this outcome was common for already disadvantaged children, because the official definition of dyslexia included the idea of “discrepancy” – that reading problems should be unexpected given a child’s other cognitive abilities. Assessing ability using IQ tests can also be biased against those from lower socioeconomic groups or learning to read in a second language. By extension, this second child is just bad at reading or lazy, or both, and not eligible to receive extra help with reading. Advertisement Two children with the same learning difficulty. One gets help, the other does not Two children with the same learning difficulty. One gets help and understanding and the other doesn’t, all because of a label. Yet this label is based on a questionable assessment. Despite trials using a wide range of cognitive processes, researchers have been unable to find meaningful ways to identify dyslexia. So, why not just help all children who struggle to read? Each has a unique combination of risk and remediation factors, but all will benefit most if we intervene when the problem first shows up, instead of waiting years for them to fail and then receive a diagnosis. Our newfound understanding of what is happening in their brains even suggests some surprisingly simple ways to help . Giving every child the best possible chance to overcome their challenge is what matters, not the label we attach to them.

science.title: The DNA is backwards on The Selfish Gene’s cover – again
science.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Don’t get it twisted Feedback is not young. We have been here on the back pages for many years, endlessly pushing a boulder up a hill and trying to take joy in the effort. This means, every so often, we are forced to repeat ourselves – because the world repeats itself. With a due sense of ennui, we turn our world-weary eyes to the cover of the new 50th anniversary edition of Richard Dawkins’s popular science classic The Selfish Gene . The title, written in all-caps, takes up most of the cover. The “I” in “SELFISH” has been replaced by a colourful little drawing of a DNA double helix. Advertisement Alas, something is awry. Geneticist Simon Fisher pointed it out on Bluesky : “You know a gene is selfish when its DNA twists the wrong way, as demonstrated by the left-handed double-helix proudly adorning the 50th Anniversary Edition of the multimillion copy bestseller on this topic.” Yes, once again we have an example of a DNA molecule being drawn, essentially, backwards. In reality, it is a right-handed double helix, but the one on the book cover is left-handed. It’s twisting the wrong way. Feedback’s mind’s eye immediately cast itself back to March 2025 , when we covered a Lego model that included many scientific and technological objects, including a sadly left-handed DNA. It turns out that The Selfish Gene ‘s art has been wrong for at least a decade. Patrick Goymer , an editor at PLOS One , shared the cover of the 40th anniversary edition on Bluesky, and it has the same left-handed DNA in place of the “I”. Feedback notes that our own copy is the 30th anniversary edition, and the DNA is correct. At some point since 2006, the DNA on the cover has flipped into a mirror universe. This little mistake would be doubly embarrassing if, say, the Nobel prize in chemistry had recently been awarded for research into these sorts of mirror molecules. Can you imagine?
